All trails are located between 800' and 1900' elevation, in a second growth forest surrounding Fall Creek, a tributary of the South Fork Alsea River. The system includes several mountain bike "flow" trails that incorporate progressive trail design and construction techniques. Flow trails within the system maximize the fun of mountain biking by combining features like rolling terrain and banked turns. Upper trails within the system have been designed to provide challenging features such as steep rock chutes and plenty of trail texture achieved through the placement of technical rock features. pages.text: Alt.Latino: Lighting candles on our sonic altar: Dolores Huerta and more : NPR Music : NPR Accessibility links Skip to main content Keyboard shortcuts for audio player Alt.Latino: Lighting candles on our sonic altar: Dolores Huerta and more : NPR Music The Mexican folk celebration of Día de los Muertos transcends borders and cultures these days. It is so widely celebrated that you can buy plastic marigolds and papél picado (the intricately cut designs on tissue paper) and even fake sugar skulls for your home altars on Amazon. And yet that popularity hasn't seemed to diminish the actual intent: an offering to the spirits of our friends and family who have passed, as a reminder that they are still in our hearts. Years ago on Alt.Latino we started a tradition of making those offerings through words and music for a Sonic Altar: songs, dedications, lots of emotions and more than a few tears. This year, we dedicate our altar to the iconic civil rights icon Dolores Huerta by returning to an Alt.Latino episode from Sept. 2017, when she mixed her passion for social justice with jazz. We also make some time for a special personal dedication, and remember some prominent Latin musicians who left us this year: Ruben Rada, Roxana Amed and Willie Colón. pages.text: Alternative Dispute Resolution Alternative Dispute Resolution Skip Navigation Within Working at Census Alternative Dispute Resolution Alternative Dispute Resolution (ADR) is an effective tool for employees, managers and supervisors in resolving various employee conflicts and disputes. It is an alternative to traditional methods of early intervention and dispute resolution. ADR provides parties the chance to present complete details of an issue in dispute, and allows the parties the opportunity to hear each other’s view points. An essential element of ADR however is that it provides parties the opportunity to identify common ground and concurrences and prepare mutually acceptable options to resolve disputed issues. These sessions, while voluntary, are highly encouraged due to their success rate, however not all situations are suitable for mediation. The advantage of mediation over more traditional complaint procedures is that it provides an environment for creative problem solving between the parties. The mediation session is private and confidential. The CADRP uses mediators from the Interagency Sharing Neutrals Program for headquarters employees and the Federal Executive Board for employees in the regions. Through the skilled assistance of the mediator, parties are encouraged to listen, be empathetic, mediate in good faith, suspend preconceived judgments, respect each other’s values, negotiate without holding to a fixed position, and focus on resolving the underlying conflict. Alternative Test Methods and Strategies to Reduce Vertebrate Animal Testing In January 2026, Administrator Zeldin signed a memo recommitting the agency to eliminate testing on mammals by the year 2035. EPA's Office of Chemical Safety and Pollution Prevention is prioritizing the development and implementation of high-quality alternatives to reduce testing on vertebrate mammals, like rabbits, mice, rats, and dogs, to align with regulatory requirements, the high bar of gold standard science and EPA's Make America Healthy Again agenda. The Toxic Substances Control Act (TSCA) directs EPA to: reduce and replace, to the extent practicable and scientifically justified, the use of vertebrate animals in the testing of chemical substances or mixtures; and promote the development and timely incorporation of alternative test methods or strategies that do not require new vertebrate animal testing. TSCA also requires EPA to maintain and regularly update a list of New Approach Methodologies (NAMs) . Close altzin Mapper since: July 08, 2024 Last map edit: May 19, 2026 小B史-陈欣恬与钱辰飞的史记 小A和小B是同班同学。初一上的时候，小A和小B在一个神秘的组织C里，这个组织在班级里坐在同一个区域，大家的关系似乎都还不错，挺开心的。一天，小B邀请小A和小C一起去她家。小C也在这个组织里，而且和小B关系很好，已经去小B家好多次了，不过小A可没去过。”明天什么安排？”小A对小B家非常好奇，且感兴趣。”你跟着我吧。”小B轻声回答，预示着这并不是一次平凡的旅途。第二天，小B带着小A和小C出发了，”我们走路去吧，会有点远。”小B对小A说，”我们先去小C家拿点东西。”，小A欣然接受，毕竟这看起来非常令人兴奋，至少对小A来说是的。路途中，欢笑一片，出现了许多载入史册的意外。”这个锁看起来不错。”小A指着马路口的一个”公安”锁箱说，”那我来把它翘掉吧”，小B此时已经疯了，她从来没有这么疯，连小C都觉得不对劲。到了小B家，小B和小C带着小A玩小B家的猫，小A很感兴趣，拿着各种东西逗它，甚至包括一个”组织C亚克力挂件”——它圆圆的，十分平整，在地上可以形成空气气垫，飞速滑动，猫咪很喜欢，小B都说它”到处都很神奇”。小C和小B很快就对她们常见的东西，包括这只猫失了兴趣，开始看B网站电视，播放着一些二次元的、第五人格的东西，小A不了解这些，只好继续和猫玩。”小A这么喜欢和猫玩。”小B说，小A虽然不是真的特别喜欢和猫玩，但迫于人情世故的无奈，只好肯定回复。晚上，小B先去厨房拆了一些”大山会员店”蛋糕给大家吃，小C和小A吃的很欢，但是小B自己没吃，毕竟平时吃太多了。小B的妈妈自称小B的朋友，曾经向小A讨要过一个”组织C亚克力挂件”，也在这天点了一些披萨给大家吃，大家还是很开心的。第二天晚上9点，小A和家人发生了矛盾，小A跑了出去，不知道该跑哪去，想起前一天刚去过小B家，便又准备跑到小B家，到了小B家门口的一条路，小A拍下路牌发到组织C的群里，组织C里的小D立刻叫醒了小B，小B开始警觉。天时不利，小A不知道小B住在那条路的哪个小区了，到处看都不对，甚至问了小C，结果小C说的”银杏小区”也不对，毕竟小C只是经常去，对地址并不熟悉。小A摸索了一阵后，最终想起自己昨天在gps定位仪上留了个位置，跟着走了过去，果然到了小B的家，上了楼，来到小B家门口。小A心慌、害怕，一到小B家门口，就左转往楼梯口走过去。万事总有疏漏，小A书包上的”组织C挂件”们互相碰撞，发出了响声，让小B听见了——小B在前一天就说过小A书包上的挂件响。小B打开了门，出来追小A，小A一会儿上楼梯，一会儿下楼梯，还时不时扭头拍小B，楼梯间很黑，小B打开手电筒，经典照片”闪闪发光”至此被小A拍下。凭借着对地形的熟悉，小B最终还是抓住了小A，甚至还归还了昨天小B落在小A家的荧光笔。事后，”组织C”群里沸沸扬扬，”今晚的事谁也不要说出去。”小B觉得很刺激。那年的最后一天，小B和小C在打电话，小A在群里发现了此事，提出可以让自己和小B再打一个电话，形成3人电话，不知怎么的，这个可怕的决定小B竟然真的决定照做，小A预料到了这个事情，提前降低了手机音量，成功接到了电话，这时已经凌晨了，大家打了一会儿电话后就散了，小A和小B都留下了电话的录音，其中的小C发出许多诡异的声音，实在太可怕，此通话最终被称为12点通话。学期末，学校带大家来到劳技中心，学校粗暴地按照学号切分，于是小C被分到了另一个项目，小A、小B和同在组织C的小D被分到了一个项目。小A其实有点想念小C，但是一看有小B，心生暖意，感觉好像也够了。小D最近似乎出现了问题，称自己”emo”，并减少参与组织C的

Search Twitter YouTube Facebook Instagram Flickr LinkedIn Alvord Desert | Oregon View Map In Full Screen While Steens Mountain looms to the west, the shimmering salt flats of the Alvord Desert unfold to the east. Tens of thousands of years ago, a lake almost 200 feet deep covered the Alvord Desert and extended southward into Nevada. The old shoreline forms terraces along the edge of the valley, and deep under the desert floor are the same lava flows that make up the top of Steens Mountain. The Alvord Desert playa can be either wet or dry depending on the time of year and is one of the largest playas in Oregon—six miles wide and 11 miles long. That means plenty of room for setting up a tent and peering up at the stars in the sky! It is a popular venue for land sailing, glider flying, land kiteboarding, and camping, among many other outdoor pursuits. Know Before You Go The Alvord Desert is accessible year-round; however, ideal conditions exist June through November, when the playa is usually dry enough for vehicular travel. pages.text: America's Road Trip: Route 66's Most Fascinating Museums Skip to main content © Paul Souders/WorldFoto, 6836 16th Ave NE, Sea/Corbis "Sixty-six is the mother road, the road of flight,” wrote John Steinbeck in his 1939 novel Grapes of Wrath . When Route 66 was first established in 1926 as one of the first official US highways, it was nearly 2,500 miles of road that connected Chicago to Los Angeles. Never before had a route captured America’s sense of freedom, adventure and opportunity quite like 66 did. Given several nicknames—including “The Main Street of America,” and “The Will Rogers Highway ”—Route 66 reigned supreme for about a quarter of a century, from the mid-1930s, when it was a migration route, until the late 1950s, when it became a major highway for postwar vacationers. With the road cutting through big cities and small towns alike, Route 66 helped small businesses thrive. Diners, motels, trading posts, gas stations, natural wonders and roadside attractions all became part of the uniquely American experience the road provided. But the Federal Highway Act of 1956 proved to be the beginning of the end of Route 66’s heyday. In response to the growing car culture of America, the law allocated money for newer, faster, better roads—like Interstate 40. These roads allowed for the near-total circumvention of Route 66. As the Mother Road saw less traffic, the small businesses alongside it died out. American Community Survey (ACS) Skip Navigation Within American Community Survey (ACS) American Community Survey (ACS) The American Community Survey (ACS) is the premier source of detailed information about the nation's people and housing. As an ongoing survey conducted by the U.S. Census Bureau since 2005, the ACS collects detailed social, economic, housing, and demographic information from a sample of households across the 50 states, the District of Columbia, and Puerto Rico. The ACS provides up-to-date information annually, which helps local officials, community leaders, and businesses make informed decisions. Covering more than 40 topics—including education, employment, income, housing, and transportation—the ACS provides crucial insights into the changing needs and conditions of communities. Its data are used for countless reasons, such as to plan roads, schools, and emergency services, and to guide the distribution of government funding. Many of the trains at the National Museum of Railroad History & Innovation are housed in the 1884 Baldwin roundhouse. Schaun Champion By Brooke Sabin Published October 20, 2026 While it’s probably best known today for crab cakes, the Orioles, and The Wire , Baltimore is a stealth heavy hitter in American history. Established in 1729 by an order of the Governor of Maryland, the city on the Chesapeake Bay is where militiamen and local citizens held off the British in the Battle of Baltimore during the War of 1812, a feat that inspired Francis Scott Key to write the poem that became the national anthem. The city is also where in 1827 the country’s first commercial railroad—the Baltimore and Ohio, or B & O—was chartered to connect the seaport with the Ohio River. It was a moment that transformed American life, says Kris Hoellen, executive director of the National Museum of Railroad History & Innovation, which was known until last summer as the B & O Railroad Museum. “It was as impactful as the modern-day Internet.” In 2027, the museum will mark the bicentennial of American railroading with a $38 million upgrade. pages.text: Americans with Disabilities Act | U.S. Department of Labor Skip to main content Americans with Disabilities Act The ADA and ODEP The ADA underpins and inspires all of ODEP's work. Through policy development, outreach and education, and technical assistance, ODEP assists both workers with disabilities and employers in understanding their protections and obligations under the law. Through its Job Accommodation Network (JAN) , ODEP provides extensive technical assistance on the reasonable accommodations provision of the ADA. Covered employers are required to provide "reasonable accommodations" to qualified job applicants and employees with disabilities. This is defined as any change or adjustment to a job, work environment, or the way things are usually done that would allow an individual with a disability to apply for a job, perform job functions, or enjoy equal access to benefits available to other employees. JAN provides expert guidance, training, and resources to individuals and employers on all aspects of accommodations at no cost. Also available are JAN publications on the ADA and related laws . Note that in the years following the ADA's passage, some courts had narrowed the definition of disability under the ADA. To address this, Congress passed the ADA Amendments Act (ADAAA) in 2008, clarifying various aspects of the law and emphasizing that the definition of disability should be interpreted broadly. AMMT is the first AM system capable of continuous variation of laser power and speed, enabled by NIST-developed pointwise AM control technology. Clara Vannucci Sometime in the early 1990s, Claudio Grossi, a 40-year-old farmer in Parma, in northern Italy, was cleaning his attic when he turned up an old sack full of seeds that he couldn’t identify. The bag, he was sure, had been left by his late great-grandfather, who’d started the farmstead around 1915. Grossi had no idea how long the seeds had been sitting there, deprived of water, soil and sun. Dry and cracked, the kernels looked so old in the palm of his hand that he doubted anything would ever sprout from them. He carried the bag down the stairs, shook the seeds out into a pile of manure and then forgot about them. To his surprise, the seeds soon sprouted a few different types of wheat. One was particularly striking: At six feet high, its plants were about twice as tall as commercial wheat. But the most remarkable feature came when it developed ears—the grain-studded parts at the top of the plant. All of the wheat types Grossi had previously seen grew only one such ear. But the tall wheat grew a full seven ears, always in the same pattern: a long one with six shorties bunched up around it like little fingers. Eloy, AWEM, Archéologie andennaise SCIENCE NEWS Ancient DNA reveals new twists in Neanderthal migration Genetic surprises pulled from 120,000-year-old bones showcase the nuanced history of this close human relative. By Maya Wei-Haas Published June 26, 2019 • 8 min read In 1856, some curious remains turned up at a limestone quarry in the Neander Valley in Germany. While the skull fragment and bones vaguely resembled those of modern humans, the brow was too robust, and the bones were too hefty. It took eight years for scientists to recognize the fossils as the first evidence of a whole other species of ancient human, Homo neanderthalensis . Further discoveries have since revealed much more about the Neanderthals, including where they lived, how they cared for their young , and perhaps even their artwork . Now, using ancient DNA extracted from a pair of European Neanderthals, scientists are getting a more detailed picture of the species’ journey across our prehistoric planet. The predecessors of the Neanderthals likely split from the ancestors of modern humans at least 500,000 years ago, and spread out across Europe and into southwest and central Asia. This Is Why They Returned to the Sea. | National Geographic Premium HISTORY & CULTURE Ancient Polynesians Took a 1,700-Year Break From Voyaging. This Is Why They Returned to the Sea. Researchers have long debated why the Pacific's most skilled navigators suddenly resumed sailing after their "Long Pause." A new study offers a clue. The 'Chasing the Rain' expedition team collects core samples on the island of Tubuai in French Polynesia. The team hopes to link past migrations of Polynesian seafarers to changes in climate, especially rainfall, and what this can tell us about the future of climate change. Shane Gross By Christina Larson Last updated August 21, 2026 The Polynesians were perhaps the ancient world’s greatest sea voyagers. They crossed vast stretches of open ocean without maps, compasses, or other navigational instruments. By Christine Dell'Amore Published November 10, 2012 • 4 min read It's no tall tale — the first complete ancient skeleton of a person with gigantism has been discovered near Rome , a new study says. At 6 feet, 8 inches (202 centimeters) tall, the man would have been a giant in third-century A.D. Rome, where men averaged about 5 and a half feet (167 centimeters) tall. By contrast, today's tallest man measures 8 feet, 3 inches (251 centimeters). Finding such skeletons is rare, because gigantism itself is extremely rare, today affecting about three people in a million worldwide. The condition begins in childhood, when a malfunctioning pituitary gland causes abnormal growth. By Maya Wei-Haas Published April 2, 2019 • 8 min read Four teeth found in a cave in the Tongzi county of southern China have scientists scratching their heads. In 1972 and 1983, researchers extracted the roughly 200,000-year-old teeth from the silty sediments of the Yanhui cave floor, initially labeling them as Homo erectus , the upright-walking hominins thought to be the first to leave Africa. Later analysis suggested they didn't quite fit with Homo erectus, but that's where the story paused for nearly two decades. Now, a study published in the Journal of Human Evolution takes a fresh look at these ancient teeth, using modern methods to examine the curious remains. The rule was introduced in the 1960s to encourage fans to attend lower league games and prevents matches from being shown on UK television between 2:45pm and 5:15pm on Saturdays. The blackout, which is enforced by Article 48 of the Uefa Statutes and is imposed by the English and Scottish football associations, comes into effect when 50% of fixtures in the top two divisions are scheduled to kick off at 3pm. The Premier League is in the middle of a record £6.7bn domestic TV deal for Sky and TNT to show up to 270 live games a season. But there could be room for change with the 3pm rule in the upcoming broadcast cycle, as the rights deals for the Premier League, EFL and SPFL all end in 2028-29. pages.text: Anger as Cas overturns ban on Russia by ice hockey's global governing body - BBC Sport Image source, Getty Images Image caption, Since the end of the Soviet Union in 1991, Russia have won the men's World Championship five times but have never claimed the women's title Published 30 October 2026 Ukraine's ice hockey federation has expressed "deep outrage" at Russia being allowed to compete in international events again. The Court of Arbitration for Sport (Cas) overturned the ban placed on Russia by the sport's global governing body, the International Ice Hockey Federation (IIHF). Russia have been suspended from competing in IIHF events since the country invaded Ukraine in February 2022 and earlier this year the IIHF ruled they would remain excluded. The Russian Ice Hockey Federation (RIHF) appealed that decision to Cas, which has upheld it following an in-person hearing at its headquarters in Lausanne, Switzerland. In a statement, the Hockey Federation of Ukraine said it "respected the authority and status of Cas". "At the same time, we express our deep outrage at this decision," it added. It said the threats, which had formed the basis of the ban, had not disappeared, adding "against this background, the decision to allow Russian teams to international hockey competitions causes special outrage". A statement from Cas , external said that arguments made by the IIHF "citing safety, security and other concerns" were "not supported by sufficient evidence". Search Twitter YouTube Facebook Instagram Flickr LinkedIn Animas Forks | Colorado View Map In Full Screen Animas Forks is located on a system of roads known as the Alpine Loop. The loop is a 65-mile (105 kilometers) system of unpaved roads which connects the small mountain towns of Lake City, Ouray, and Silverton. Most of the land in the area is managed by either the U.S. Forest Service or the Bureau of Land Management. The Alpine Loop is visited by over 100,000 people each year. Animas Forks, at an elevation of 11,200 feet (3,400 meter), is more than two miles (3 kilometers) above sea level. The unimproved road from Silverton to Animas Forks is passable in summer by two-wheel drive vehicles. The road beyond Animas Forks over Engineer Pass to Lake City may require four-wheel drive. The town's first log cabin was built in 1873 and by 1876 the community had become a bustling mining community. At that time the town contained 30 cabins, a hotel, a general store, a saloon, and a post office. pages.text: Annual Survey of Public Employment & Payroll Summary Report: 2025 Annual Survey of Public Employment & Payroll Summary Report: 2025 Skip Navigation Within Census Bureau Library Annual Survey of Public Employment & Payroll Summary Report: 2025 April 16, 2026 Written by: ROSS JACOBSON, JAMI SEGAL, JENNIFER WENNING, and SEAN WILBURN Report Number: G25-ASPEP Introduction Download Annual Survey of Public Employment & Payroll Summary Report: 2025 [PDF - <1.0 MB] In March 2025, state and local governments employed 20.3 million people, an increase of 1.4 percent from the 2024 figure of 20.0 million. Nationally, local government workers comprised the majority of the state and local government workforce with 14.7 million employees (72.2 percent). Full-time employment by state governments increased by 2.7 percent to 4.1 million, while full-time employment by local governments increased 1.2 percent to 11.7 million. The number of part-time state government employees increased 0.8 percent to 1.5 million. Part-time local government employees increased 0.8 percent to 3.0 million.
